chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram who uses a miswak (tooth-stick). He said: 'Yes, and he should not cause bleeding.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.وَلَا يُدْمِي: And he should not cause bleeding

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to use a miswak for oral hygiene?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of using a miswak while in Ihram is contingent upon avoiding bleeding, a condition rooted in the juristic principle that blood loss may invalidate the state of consecration or require expiation. This ruling highlights the nuanced balance between maintaining personal hygiene (Sunnah) and preserving the sanctity of the ritual state, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to prophetic traditions during Hajj.
